name: Acoustic Concert Guitar
shortDescription: Six-stringed plucked chordophone with hollow resonant chamber and internal bracing.
description: The classical acoustic guitar produces sound through the transverse vibration of coupled tensioned strings, which transmit vibrational kinetic energy through the bridge and soundboard into the internal Helmholtz air cavity.
historicalOrigins: Evolved from the Renaissance vihuela and Baroque guitar into the modern Spanish fan-braced guitar designed by Antonio de Torres in the 1850s.
acousticPrinciples: Transverse string standing waves defined by Mersenne's laws: f = (1/2L)√(T/μ)
Bridge serves as acoustic transducer coupling strings to the top soundboard
Soundboard functions as a dipole radiator while soundhole provides Helmholtz cavity resonance around 100 Hz

characteristics.timbralColor: Warm, woody, articulate, rich in lower-mid harmonics
characteristics.orchestralRole: Harmonic foundation, soloist voice, rhythmic comping

soundDNA.exciter: Finger pluck or plectrum displacing tensioned steel/nylon string
soundDNA.resonator: Solid Sitka spruce soundboard with rosewood back, sides, and Helmholtz air cavity
soundDNA.harmonics: Integer harmonic series (f, 2f, 3f...) with rapid decay in high frequencies
soundDNA.attackDecay: Sharp attack (~5ms) followed by exponential decay with 2–5s sustain
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Warm woody fundamental with delicate shimmering upper partials
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Directional forward radiation from soundboard with omnidirectional low-end from soundhole

body.label: Resonant Soundbox
body.function: Amplifies low and midrange frequencies through resonant wood plates and enclosed air volume.

characteristics.material: Solid Sitka Spruce top, East Indian Rosewood back & sides
characteristics.mechanism: Flexural plate vibration and Helmholtz air resonance

soundboard.label: Soundboard (Top Plate)
soundboard.function: Vibrates in complex eigenmodes to convert string energy into airborne sound pressure waves.

neck.label: Neck & Headstock
neck.function: Supports string tension of 60–80 kg and provides structural alignment.

characteristics.material: Honduran Mahogany with dual-action truss rod

fretboard.label: Fretboard & Frets
fretboard.function: Divides string lengths into tempered semitones by setting vibrating boundary conditions.

strings.label: Tensioned Strings
strings.function: Primary oscillators that establish standing wave frequencies when plucked.

characteristics.material: Phosphor bronze wound over high-carbon steel core

bridge.label: Bridge & Saddle
bridge.function: Transmits mechanical rocking motion from strings to soundboard with impedance matching.

characteristics.material: Dense Ebony bridge with bone saddle
characteristics.mechanism: Mechanical rocking lever and impedance transformer

tuning_pegs.label: Tuning Machine Heads
tuning_pegs.function: Adjusts string tension (T) to calibrate fundamental frequency via worm gear mechanisms.

characteristics.material: Die-cast brass gears with pearloid buttons

soundhole.label: Soundhole & Rosette
soundhole.function: Vent for internal acoustic air piston; tunes Helmholtz resonant peak around A2/G2.

characteristics.material: Circular aperture with wood mosaic inlay rosette

followTheSound.title: String Pluck (Oscillation)
followTheSound.explanation: A player displaces the string, introducing potential energy. Releasing it creates counter-propagating transverse wave pulses.

followTheSound.title: Boundary Termination
followTheSound.explanation: The nut and fret pinch the string, fixing end nodes and defining the effective vibrating length L.

followTheSound.title: Acoustic Transduction
followTheSound.explanation: String tension variations exert periodic downward and rocking forces upon the saddle and bridge.

followTheSound.title: Soundboard Radiation
followTheSound.explanation: The bridge drives the spruce soundboard into flexural eigenmodes, displacing large volumes of ambient air.

followTheSound.title: Internal Cavity & Soundhole
followTheSound.explanation: Internal acoustic reflections reinforce the bass through the soundhole via Helmholtz resonance, emitting full-spectrum audio.
